newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Camargo Correa buys Brazil cement firm.
newsitem.headline: Camargo Correa buys Brazil cement firm.

text.p: Brazilian construction group Camargo Correa Industrial said Wednesday it had bought 97.29 percent of cement maker Cimento Caue and expects to double, to 10 percent, its share of the local cement market.
"With the acquisition of Caue's two cement plants and brand name, Camargo Correa Industrial should double its market share in the local cement industry," the group said in a statement.
A spokesman for the group refused to reveal the terms of the Caue deal.
Camargo Correa Industrial is one of 29 subsidiaries of the Camargo Correa group, which holds five percent of the country's cement market.
The acquisition of Caue is part of the group's strategic plan to invest in the cement industry and offers "great sinergy" with its core construction and engineering businesses, Camargo Correa said.
The deal also will allow Camargo Correa Industrial to consolidate and expand its presence in Brazil's southeast, where it has other cement plants. Cimento Caue is based in Minas Gerais state.

Camargo Correa Industrial, which also owns local cement maker Cimento Portland Eldorado, has annual revenues of about $140 million and operates cement plants in Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Sao Paulo and Mato Grosso do Sul states.
Annual revenues at Camargo Correa group total roughly 1.8 billion reais ($1.69 billion).
